source.title: Under the Shadow of Babel: How Language Shapes Reasoning in LLMs
source.authors: Chenxi Wang; Yixuan Zhang; Lang Gao; Zixiang Xu; Zirui Song; Yanbo Wang; Xiuying Chen

record.tranche_reason: Measures cross-language and cross-structure similarity using SVCCA and hidden-state cosine similarity, providing a conceptual test of input-dependence in measured alignment. It does not test alignment growth with model scale.
record.gate_note: The study reports BICAUSE reasoning accuracies and attention-allocation differences, but these do not themselves measure representational alignment. Rows below cover the reported similarity measurements. Accuracy results are not rows for the claim versions because accuracy is not a similarity or alignment measure.
record.test_reason: All similarity results compare inputs within one model (Qwen1.5-1.8B-Chat): English vs Chinese, forward vs reversed chains. No version is about this. V1-V5 concern alignment between different models or seeds. V6 concerns how between-model convergence depends on metric or inputs. No comparison across models, seeds, modalities or mapping is made. The SVCCA scores also compare 24x3 attention-ratio trajectories, not representations. This is a related construct: within-model cross-lingual representation similarity. Accuracy results for other models are not alignment measures.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but incomplete. The authors also conclude that LLMs show typologically aligned attention patterns (more on causes and initial connectives in Chinese). They also find models rigidly apply language-specific causal-order preferences, which degrades accuracy on reversed Chinese chains. And when reasoning succeeds, hidden representations converge across languages and structures in late layers.
record.recipe_differences: Measures attention-trajectory similarity with SVCCA and hidden-state cosine similarity on bilingual causal-reasoning inputs; it does not reproduce the original sources' model-scale convergence measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported similarity varies with language and causal sentence structure; cosine analysis is restricted to pairs of inputs for which both predictions are correct.

fits_no_version.finding: In Qwen1.5-1.8B-Chat, hidden states at the final causal token are most similar for English vs Chinese forward inputs and least similar for Chinese forward vs reversed in middle layers. All pairs converge to relatively high cosine in the final layers, for correctly answered samples only (Fig. 5). Attention-trajectory SVCCA is 0.73 for English vs Chinese forward, 0.64 for English forward vs reversed, and ~0.46 for Chinese forward vs reversed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within one multilingual LLM, representations of semantically equivalent inputs in different languages or word orders converge in late layers, while middle layers depend on surface structure.

record.problems: The representation analysis is centered on Qwen1.5-1.8B-Chat; the cosine analysis conditions on both inputs being answered correctly. The study covers only Chinese and English. Figure 5 gives no numerical cosine values, and the reported SVCCA comparison concerns attention trajectories rather than hidden-state representations.

untested.parts: No comparison of representations between independently trained models, nor with scale.
No vision-language or paired image-caption alignment.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation test between models.
No recurrence of features or circuits across models.
No between-model convergence measure, so dependence on metric or inputs is not tested.
No measurement of the degree of between-model alignment, a plateau, or its causes.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V6 'tested' status is wrong. V6 is about measured convergence between models, but every comparison here is between inputs within a single model. The SVCCA is applied to attention-ratio trajectories (24x3 RCAR matrices), not to hidden representations. Other models (Llama-3.2, Mistral-7B, Qwen1.5 7B-72B) appear only in accuracy tables and attention heatmaps, with no cross-model similarity.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure whether alignment between independently trained models rises with model size or capability.
Uses Chinese and English text inputs, not vision-language models or paired images and captions; does not test alignment as both models improve.
No comparison across random seeds or measurement of shared features or subspaces across same-architecture models.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability test.
Does not test recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across models.

Tests dependence on language and sentence structure with SVCCA and cosine similarity, but not alternative similarity metrics on the same representation, metric settings such as neighbour count, or out-of-distribution inputs.
Does not test whether alignment plateaus or is explained by shared training data or objectives rather than a shared model of reality.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Comparisons across forward and reversed input structures
reader_labels.reason: Similarity differs by input structure: the Chinese forward/reversed SVCCA score is around 0.46 versus 0.73 for English-forward/Chinese-forward, and the text reports the Chinese pair has the lowest middle-layer cosine similarity (R1-R5). This supports dependence on the inputs and structures compared.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Correctly answered paired inputs in the final layers
reader_labels.reason: The authors report relatively high final-layer cosine similarity for all plotted input forms, so the structural differences do not eliminate similarity in this tested, correctness-filtered setting (R8).
